newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian union leader killed in mafia-style shooting.
newsitem.headline: Indian union leader killed in mafia-style shooting.

text.p: Prominent Indian trade union leader Datta Samant, who once brought powerful industrialists to their knees, was shot dead in a Bombay suburb by four unidentified gunmen on Thursday, police said.
The mafia-style killing sent shock waves through India's labour movement, and union leaders said they would organise demonstrations to protest Samant's death.
Police said Samant and his son were travelling in a jeep when the attackers opened fire from a motor-rickshaw in the central suburb of Powai.
Samant, 65, was shot in the head. He was declared dead on arrival at a private clinic.
Samant's chauffeur, also injured in the attack, was in hospital while the union leader's son escaped unhurt.
A police official said trade union rivalry may have been behind the murder.
"Trade union rivalry cannot be ruled out," said joint police commissioner R.S. Sharma.
Business leaders have complained in the past that organised crime was spreading through trade unions and the textile industry in the city, which is India's commercial capital.
Samant was also a critic of the mafia-style gangs.
Police launched a hunt for the killers and said they were prepared to quell any violent protests from workers who owed allegiance to the various unions Samant led.
A doctor who gave up his profession for militant trade unionism, Samant shot into the spotlight in the early 1980s when he led a two-year-long textile strike in Bombay.
He later became a member of the Maharashtra state legislature and moved to the national parliament.
Last year he led a strike at carmaker PAL-Peugeot Ltd.

"It is a reprehensible act to smother the voice of the people by violence and terror and it should be condemned by one and all," said Sharad Pawar, a former chief minister of Maharashtra and now leader of the Congress party in the Lok Sabha (lower house of parliament).
Prabhakar Sanjgiri, a leader of CITU (Centre of Indian Trade Unions) said his organisation would contact other trade unions to organise protests against Samant's killing.
"I demand that those involved in it should be found out and booked immediately. It is an obvious attempt to eliminate a militant trade unionist. It's a great loss to the workers movement."
